title: Does Validation Loss Predict Real-Robot Success? Evidence from Four Imitation-Learning Policies on a Low-Cost Arm
title_zh: 验证损失能预测真实机器人成功率吗？来自低成本机械臂上四种模仿学习策略的证据
abstract: Held-out validation loss is the standard offline signal for choosing checkpoints and comparing models, but its relation to closed-loop success on a real robot is rarely measured. We measure it for ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA and $π_{0.5}$ (action expert only), trained on nested subsets of 12 to 200 demonstrations of a pick-and-place task on an SO-101 arm. We score 82 checkpoints on 25 held-out demonstrations, with each policy's training loss and with the error of the actions it outputs, and compare the scores with 930 bench rollouts. We also score all 700 intermediate checkpoints of 70 training runs, and recover the ball positions of every training, held-out and bench episode from the front camera. Within each policy, hold-out action error correlates with bench success (Spearman $ρ$ from -0.23 to -0.88), but no more strongly than the number of training episodes alone, and not at all among seeds trained on the same data. Across policies the ranking is inverted ($ρ$ = +0.90 at 200 episodes): the policy with the lowest hold-out error succeeded in 3 of 110 rollouts. The most common failure, the arm never leaving its rest pose, ended 96% of rollouts for Diffusion Policy trained on untrimmed demonstrations and 47% for SmolVLA, and cannot occur in a hold-out set made of demonstrations. Among rollouts in which the arm moved, SmolVLA's hold-out action error predicts success well ($ρ$ = -0.81). For the diffusion and flow-matching policies, hold-out loss rises two- to five-fold during training while hold-out action error falls by up to 29%. Held-out metrics are a sound diagnostic of learning but no substitute for evaluation on the robot, and we recommend reporting initiation failure and success among started rollouts as separate bench outcomes.
abstract_zh: 留出验证损失是选择检查点和比较模型的标准离线信号，但其与真实机器人闭环成功率的关系很少被测量。我们针对 ACT、Diffusion Policy、SmolVLA 和 $π_{0.5}$（仅动作专家）在 SO-101 机械臂上抓取放置任务的 12 到 200 个演示的嵌套子集上进行训练，并测量了这种关系。我们用 25 个留出演示对 82 个检查点进行评分，评分依据包括每个策略的训练损失及其输出动作的误差，并将评分与 930 次基准 rollout 进行比较。我们还对 70 次训练运行的所有 700 个中间检查点进行评分，并从前置摄像头恢复每个训练、留出和基准回合的球位置。在每个策略内，留出动作误差与基准成功率相关（Spearman $ρ$ 从 -0.23 到 -0.88），但不比仅训练回合数更强，且在相同数据训练的种子间完全不相关。跨策略时排名反转（200 回合时 $ρ$ = +0.90）：留出误差最低的策略在 110 次 rollout 中仅成功 3 次。最常见的失败是机械臂从未离开静止姿态，这在 Diffusion Policy 使用未修剪演示训练时占 rollout 的 96%，在 SmolVLA 中占 47%，且不可能发生在由演示构成的留出集中。在机械臂移动的 rollout 中，SmolVLA 的留出动作误差能很好地预测成功（$ρ$ = -0.81）。对于扩散和流匹配策略，训练期间留出损失上升两到五倍，而留出动作误差下降高达 29%。留出指标是学习的有力诊断工具，但不能替代在机器人上的评估，我们建议将启动失败和已启动 rollout 中的成功率作为单独的基准结果报告。
tldr_zh: 验证损失不能可靠预测真实机器人成功率，需直接评估。
cover_zh: 验证损失低反而成功率崩？机器人策略评估的真相
